title: Greedy (exchange argument, sorting-by-criterion, scheduling)
relevance: High — OAs and Div2 A–C constantly ask “sort by the right key, then take locally optimal choices”; interval / deadline / pairing variants dominate interview greedy.
company_notes: Max meetings / min removals / burst balloons → sort intervals by end (Movie Festival / LC 435 / LC 452). Reach-the-end / min jumps / circular gas → frontier or tank scan (Jump Game family / Gas Station)—common FAANG phone-screen. Assign cookies / rescue boats / light+heavy under capacity → sort + two pointers (Assign Cookies / Ferris Wheel). Finish jobs before deadlines / maximize score under time → sort by deadline or duration, often with a heap to drop the worst (Tasks & Deadlines / Course Schedule III / Potions).

phases.goal: Establish that the problem is greedy: fixed-priority local choices after sorting, not DP or heavy search.

must_hit.point: A greedy problem builds an optimal answer by repeatedly making a locally best choice under a fixed priority (earliest finish, smallest cost, largest gain, or a custom comparator from a 2-element swap).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names locally optimal choices under a fixed priority / comparator rather than exploring all subsets.

must_hit.point: Recognize greedy when the statement maximizes/minimizes a count or sum under constraints and a sort plus one left-to-right pass (sometimes with a heap) feels plausible.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Points at max/min under constraints plus sort + single forward pass (optional heap) as the cue.

must_hit.point: OA/interview disguises include interval end-time scheduling (meetings / removals / arrows), reach/tank scans (Jump Game / Gas Station), sort+two-pointer pairing (cookies / boats), and deadline/duration scheduling often with a heap.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maps the prompt to one of: sort-by-end intervals, frontier/tank scan, pairing two pointers, or deadline/duration + heap.

probes: What in the statement suggests a fixed sort key plus a single left-to-right greedy pass rather than DP?
Is the priority earliest finish, smallest cost, largest gain, or a swap-derived comparator—and how do you know?

hints.1: Ask whether a locally best choice under one priority could build the whole answer.
hints.2: Look for maximize/minimize a count/sum under constraints where sort + one forward pass (maybe a heap) feels natural.
hints.3: Name the priority (earliest finish / cost / gain / swap comparator) and the OA cousin: intervals-by-end, Jump/Gas scan, cookies pairing, or deadline heap.

phases.goal: Pick the right comparator and justify it with an exchange argument or domination before coding.

must_hit.point: Prove the key with an exchange argument: any optimal solution can be swapped toward the greedy order without worsening, or every rejected alternative is dominated.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States you can transform any optimal into the greedy order by swaps without loss, or that rejected picks are dominated.

must_hit.point: For interval / activity selection, sort by end (or by deadline / duration) then take one forward pass—Movie Festival is the canonical earliest-ending proof; Non-overlapping Intervals is the same idea as min removals.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says sort intervals by end time then greedily keep non-overlapping (or drop conflicts / stab overlapping groups).

must_hit.point: Exchange-argument scheduling template (Tasks and Deadlines): compare two adjacent items; if swapping never hurts, that comparator defines an optimal order—here sort by duration.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions adjacent-swap exchange and duration order for Tasks & Deadlines–style scheduling.

must_hit.point: Stretch variants keep the same idea with more machinery: multi-resource earliest-ending + multiset (Movie Festival II), reverse/latest-possible packing (Petya's Exams), or sort by deadline then drop the longest via a max-heap when overdue (Course Schedule III).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names multiset of end times, reverse deadline packing, or deadline-sort + heap-drop-longest as the stretch move.

probes: What do you sort by, and how would an exchange argument show that order is optimal?
For intervals, why earliest-ending rather than earliest-starting?

hints.1: Name a sort key before proposing DP or search.
hints.2: Argue adjacent swap / exchange: moving toward the greedy order never worsens the answer.
hints.3: Intervals → sort by end + forward keep; Tasks & Deadlines → sort by duration via exchange; stretch → multiset ends, reverse packing, or deadline + drop-longest heap.

phases.goal: Code the concrete greedy scan: sort, then pairing, reach/tank, constructible prefix, or multiset rooms.

must_hit.point: Pairing template: sort both sides then two-pointer assign the greediest feasible match (Assign Cookies / Ferris Wheel lightest+heaviest under capacity / boats).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes sorting then two pointers matching lightest with heaviest or next feasible cookie/child.

must_hit.point: Reach / tank invariants: Jump Game maintains a farthest-reach index; Gas Station resets the start when the tank goes below 0, with the exchange that if you fail at i, no start in the failed segment works.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions farthest-reach scan and/or tank reset when tank < 0 plus the failed-segment start argument.

must_hit.point: Missing Coin Sum constructible prefix: maintain reach and accept the next coin iff it is ≤ reach+1; if the next coin is > reach+1, that sum is impossible.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States the reach / reach+1 acceptance rule for the next coin.

must_hit.point: Multi-resource scheduling (Room Allocation / Movie Festival II): assign free rooms via a multiset of end times while keeping earliest-ending order.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses a multiset (or heap) of finishing times to reuse the earliest free resource.

probes: Walk through how you would implement sort + two-pointer pairing for lightest+heaviest under a capacity.
How do you maintain the Jump Game farthest reach or the Gas Station tank reset in one pass?

hints.1: After sorting, say what one left-to-right pass tracks.
hints.2: Pairing → two pointers; Jump → farthest index; Gas → reset start when tank < 0; coins → reach vs reach+1.
hints.3: Also: Room Allocation / Movie Festival II free rooms via multiset of end times.

phases.goal: Catch wrong comparators and cases where greedy must be abandoned for DP.

must_hit.point: Abandon greedy for general coin change and 0/1 knapsack—those need DP (USACO Guide “when greedy fails”); Hit the Lottery only shows when canonical denominations make coin greedy safe.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Refuses blind coin/knapsack greedy and contrasts canonical denominations vs general coin DP.

must_hit.point: Wrong interval comparator (e.g. sorting by start instead of end) breaks activity selection / min-removals / arrows—all of which share the sort-by-end family.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Insists on sorting by end time for Movie Festival / LC 435 / LC 452 style prompts.

must_hit.point: Skipping the proof habit—failing to argue that any optimal solution can be transformed into the greedy one without loss—leaves a plausible but unjustified local heuristic.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives an exchange or domination sketch, not only “sort then take best.”

probes: When would you refuse greedy and switch to DP on a coin or knapsack-flavored prompt?
What goes wrong if you schedule intervals sorted by start time instead of end time?

hints.1: Ask whether the denominations/items are a known greedy-safe case.
hints.2: General coin change and 0/1 knapsack → DP; intervals → must sort by end.
hints.3: Also demand an exchange/transform-to-greedy proof, not just a local rule of thumb.

tradeoffs.topic: Canonical-denomination coin greedy vs general coin DP
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Hit the Lottery–style canonical denominations can make greedy safe; general coin change needs DP—know when greedy fails before coding a denomination grab.

tradeoffs.topic: Sort-by-end interval greedy vs other interval orders
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Max meetings, min removals, and arrows-to-burst-balloons all use sort by end time then a forward pass; sorting by start (or another key) is the usual wrong comparator.

tradeoffs.topic: Single-resource earliest-ending vs multi-resource multiset scheduling
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Movie Festival is one person earliest-ending; Movie Festival II / Room Allocation keep earliest-ending but track free resources with a multiset of end times.

tradeoffs.topic: Sort-by-duration exchange vs deadline-sort + heap drop
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Tasks and Deadlines sorts by duration via adjacent-swap exchange; Course Schedule III / Potions-style prompts sort by deadline (or take positives) and use a heap to dump the worst when the schedule breaks.

tradeoffs.topic: Two-pointer pairing vs skill-matched greedy matching
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Cookies / Ferris Wheel pair after sorting with two pointers under a capacity/greediest-feasible rule; BerSU Ball is sort + greedy matching within difference 1—same family, different feasibility predicate.

gotchas.trap: Applying coin/knapsack greedy when the problem is general coin change or 0/1 knapsack.
gotchas.correction: Switch to DP; only treat denomination greedy as safe when the setting is canonical (Hit the Lottery lesson / USACO “when greedy fails”).

gotchas.trap: Sorting intervals by start time for activity selection, min removals, or arrows.
gotchas.correction: Sort by end time, then keep non-overlapping / drop conflicts / stab overlapping groups (Movie Festival / LC 435 / LC 452).

gotchas.trap: On Missing Coin Sum, accepting coins without the reach+1 rule.
gotchas.correction: Maintain reach; accept next iff ≤ reach+1; if next coin > reach+1, that sum is impossible.

gotchas.trap: On Gas Station, restarting anywhere after a failure without the segment exchange.
gotchas.correction: Reset start when tank < 0; if you fail at i, no start in the failed segment works.

gotchas.trap: Treating Jump Game as needing DP/BFS when a farthest-reach scan suffices.
gotchas.correction: Maintain the reachable frontier (farthest index); Jump Game II extends the same invariant with range/BFS-layer greedy for min jumps.

gotchas.trap: Claiming a sort key is optimal without an exchange or domination argument.
gotchas.correction: Compare adjacent items (Tasks & Deadlines template) or show any optimal can be swapped into the greedy order without loss.
